scenarios.title: Repair the login file Bash actually reads
scenarios.summary: Trace login file selection and repair exported settings without losing local values.
scenarios.objective: For every supplied login sample, export APP_NAME as the supplied PROJECT followed by -app. Preserve supplied PROJECT and SITE, including their values and export attributes; retain the system profile’s exported BASE value. Keep LOCAL_NOTE=only-here in sessions that select .bash_profile, without exporting it; leave it unset in fallback sessions. Keep startup quiet, preserve the supplied /work/keep.txt sample files, and let every session and the supplied new-program report finish successfully.

scenarios.explanation: Repair the first personal file that actually runs, then preserve the fallbacks for sessions where it is absent. The system profile runs first, local values stay local, and exported values reach the supplied new program. Printing the desired report cannot replace the required settings.
hints: Check which personal file is first present in each sample; editing .profile alone cannot override .bash_profile.
An assignment changes a value in this shell. export controls whether the new program receives it. Preserve BASE and the local note.
Derive APP_NAME from the supplied PROJECT instead of copying one sample’s name; do not export LOCAL_NOTE.
scenarios.simplifications: Original bounded in-process startup model around evaluator 17. Fixed virtual HOME /home/learner; supplied readable files, explicit session modes and literal BASH_ENV selection only. Settings, exports, literal-format printf and simple conditions; no source/dot, aliases, history, PATH search, arbitrary files or real profiles. Selection is checked against the Bash manual; fixed developer comparisons cover sourced settings, not automatic host login startup. See SHELL_STARTUP_SUBSET.md.

scenarios.title: Keep interactive greetings out of script output
scenarios.summary: Separate interactive output from settings used by a script.
scenarios.objective: For both interactive non-login samples, print exactly Ready followed by a newline and export APP_NAME as the supplied PROJECT followed by -app. For the script with a selected /work/startup.env file, export that same derived APP_NAME but print nothing during startup. For the script without a selected startup file, preserve the supplied APP_NAME unchanged and print nothing. Preserve PROJECT, its export attribute and the supplied /work/keep.txt sample files. Every session and the supplied new-program report must finish successfully.

hints: Read the session type and selected files. .bashrc belongs to non-login interactive startup, not the script samples.

Retain a derived APP_NAME in both relevant files, export it, and keep the Ready greeting only for the interactive session.
